chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

If a man is struck on his head and his tongue becomes impaired, then the letters of the alphabet are presented to him; whatever speech he is unable to articulate clearly, for that there is blood-money for him in proportion to that injury.

key_terms.حُرُوفُ ٱلْمُعْجَمِ: the letters of the alphabet used to test speech ability
key_terms.لِسَانُهُ: his tongue, meaning his faculty of speech
key_terms.ٱلْقِصَاصِ: measured requital or proportional legal assessment

ai.seo_question: How is diyah assessed for speech impairment caused by a head injury in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for assessing compensation when a person suffers speech impairment after a head injury. The degree of liability is determined by testing which letters he can no longer pronounce, and compensation is assigned according to the extent of the loss.
